name: rights_issue_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: When a company announces a rights issue, the stock price should theoretically drop by the theoretical ex-rights price (TERP) on the ex-date. However, empirical evidence from NSE shows that the actual price adjustment is often incomplete on the ex-date — stocks either overshoot (drop more than TERP implies) or undershoot (drop less). By computing the TERP-implied price and comparing it to the actual opening price on the ex-date, we can identify mispricing. Overshoot = buy (price dropped too much, will recover toward TERP). Undershoot = short (price hasn't fully adjusted, will drop further toward TERP). The inefficiency exists because TERP computation requires understanding of rights issue mechanics, and the ex-date adjustment is confused by retail investors who don't understand dilution.
universe: NSE-listed stocks with active rights issue (ex-date within trading session)
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹25 Cr; rights issue ratio must be at least 1:10 (material dilution); F&O listed preferred

indicators.name: Volume_Ratio
indicators.params: volume / ADV(20) * 375 (normalized for time of day)

conditions: Mispricing_Bps < -30 (stock opened > 30 bps below TERP — overshoot, cheap)
Volume_Ratio > 1.5 in first 15 bars (active trading, not illiquid)
NIFTY_50 not down > 1% (market not in broad selloff)
long.confirmation: Price starts recovering: close > open of ex-date after initial dip AND close > VWAP_ExDate

conditions: Mispricing_Bps > 30 (stock opened > 30 bps above TERP — undershoot, expensive)
short.confirmation: Price starts declining: close < open of ex-date AND close < VWAP_ExDate

entry.entry_price: market order after confirmation (typically within first 30 bars)

exit.target: Close converges to TERP (Mispricing_Bps → 0, abs < 10 bps)
exit.stop_loss: Mispricing worsens to -60 bps for longs / +60 bps for shorts (double entry deviation)
exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: 180 bars (3 hours) — rights mispricing should correct within first half of session

risk.position_sizing: ₹75K per trade due to event-specific uncertainty

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; high VIX makes rights issue mispricing harder to distinguish from general volatility
filters.time_filter: Entry only in first 60 bars of ex-date session; after that, mispricing is likely intentional
filters.volume_filter: Volume_Ratio > 1.5 (sufficient trading activity to confirm price discovery)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must be within ± 1% of previous close (neutral market environment)
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 10 bps (wider than usual on ex-date is acceptable)
filters.event_filter: Must be a rights issue ex-date specifically; not applicable to bonus/split ex-dates
other_filters: Rights issue must be underwritten (ensures completion); avoid unsubscribed rights issues

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — rights issues are infrequent (5-15 per year among liquid stocks); each event requires manual TERP computation; low competition from systematic traders

weaknesses: Rights issues are extremely infrequent in liquid stocks — the strategy may generate 0-1 trades per month, making it impractical as a standalone strategy
TERP computation assumes the market fully values the rights subscription — but if the market believes the rights issue signals financial distress, the 'correct' post-rights price may be below TERP
Wider spreads on ex-date (8-15 bps typical) eat into the mispricing edge; actual slippage may be 5+ bps per side rather than the usual 3 bps
prior_art: Rights issue pricing in Eckbo & Masulis (1992); Indian rights issue studies by NSE Centre for Excellence in Market Microstructure; TERP methodology in corporate finance textbooks
notes: This strategy is best operated as a special-situations overlay to a primary systematic strategy. TERP calculation must account for the rights ratio and rights price precisely. Consider using options to hedge the position if the stock is in F&O.
